question: Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle. Extend side \(\overline{AB}\) beyond \(B\) to a point \(B'\) so that \(BB' = 3 \cdot AB.\) Similarly, extend side \(\overline{BC}\) beyond \(C\) to a point \(C'\) so that \(CC' = 3 \cdot BC,\) and extend side \(\overline{CA}\) beyond \(A\) to a point \(A'\) so that \(AA' = 3 \cdot CA.\) What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle A'B'C'\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)
solution:
The extensions give bases three times as long as the original sides. Comparing triangles with the same altitude therefore lets us express their areas as multiples of the original area.

Write \([PQR]\) for the area of \(\triangle PQR\), and let \(X=[ABC]\). Connect \(C\) to \(B'\), \(A\) to \(C'\), and \(B\) to \(A'\).

Triangles \(BB'C\) and \(ABC\) have bases \(BB'\) and \(AB\) on the same line and share vertex \(C\), so they have the same altitude. Since \(BB'=3AB\), we get \([BB'C]=3X\). Applying the same comparison around the triangle gives
\[
[BB'C]=[CC'A]=[AA'B]=3X.
\]
Next, triangles \(AA'C'\) and \(ACC'\) share vertex \(C'\), with bases \(AA'\) and \(AC\) on the same line. Since \(AA'=3AC\),
\[
[AA'C']=3[ACC']=3(3X)=9X.
\]
Cycling the vertex labels gives \([CC'B']=9X\) and \([BB'A']=9X\) as well.

To account for the whole outer triangle, its extended side segments separate it into \(ABC\) and the three triangles \(AA'B'\), \(BB'C'\), and \(CC'A'\). Each of these surrounding triangles is split by one of our added segments into a \(3X\) piece and a \(9X\) piece. These pieces have disjoint interiors and fill the outer triangle. Hence
\[
[A'B'C']=X+3(3X+9X)=37X.
\]
The requested ratio is \(\boxed{37:1}\), choice \(\textbf{(E)}\).

edges.reason: Congruence properties motivate the converse-style SAS criterion; the SAS proof step itself uses its givens and congruence definition without invoking the property theorem.
Prior SSS exploration models how to test minimal determining conditions, while SAS can be introduced independently and need not use SSS.

Triangle classification helps recognize where an altitude may lie. The area relation and a supplied base/height can be used across all triangle types without first sorting them as acute, right or obtuse.
edges.scope: locating heights in right and obtuse triangles

edges.reason: The target explicitly states that the triangle has half the area of an equal-base equal-height parallelogram. Parallelogram-area meaning is needed for that specified comparison.

The criterion explicitly permits triangles OR rectangles. Both external reviews turn that alternative into an unconditional requirement, but an L-shaped orthogonal figure can be split entirely into rectangles. Preserve triangle area as a component of the triangular-piece route without making every composite-area task use it.
edges.scope: Calculating triangular pieces in a triangular partition of a composite area
